title: Beef Tacos
subtitle: Crispy shells, spiced ground beef, all the toppings
excerpt: Crispy corn shells filled with well-seasoned ground beef, topped with shredded lettuce, cheddar, soured cream, and salsa. The beef cooks in under ten minutes and the result beats a takeaway on every count.
sourceNotes: Tex-Mex hard-shell tacos: a US diner and home-kitchen standard drawing on Mexican taco tradition adapted for the Anglo-American pantry. Recipe derived from classic American home-cooking sources including Fannie Farmer's The Boston Cooking-School Cook Book and regional Tex-Mex canon.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The beef filling keeps refrigerated for 3 days and reheats well in a pan.

glossaryTerms.definition: A regional American cuisine that blends Mexican cooking traditions with Texas ranch-cooking, known for dishes like tacos, enchiladas, and fajitas made with widely available US pantry staples.

content.text: Beef tacos are crispy corn shells filled with spiced ground beef and finished with cold toppings at the table. The beef is quick, the assembly takes two minutes, and the result is endlessly customisable. These are the
hard-shell version: the shells go in the oven to warm while the beef cooks, so everything hits the table hot.
A large frying pan is all you need. Hard-shell corn taco shells are sold in most supermarkets; warm them in the oven for 3-4 minutes at 180°C so they stay crisp.
Heat the oven to 180°C. Place the taco shells on a baking tray and set aside.
Heat {{vegetable-oil}} of oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat. Add {{onion}} onion and cook for 5 minutes until softened.
Add {{garlic}} of crushed garlic and cook for 1 minute. Add {{beef-mince}} of beef mince and break it up with a spoon. Cook for 5-6 minutes, stirring occasionally, until browned through.

Stir in {{chilli-powder}} of chilli powder, {{cumin-ground}} of cumin, {{smoked-paprika}} of smoked paprika, and {{tomato-puree}} of tomato purée. Cook for 2 minutes, adding a splash of water if the mixture looks dry. Season with salt.
While the beef finishes, put the taco shells in the oven for 3-4 minutes.
Set out the toppings: grated cheddar, soured cream, diced tomato, coriander, lime wedges, and jalapeño if using. Everyone fills their own shells at the table.

items.symptom: The beef is dry and crumbly
items.cause: Mince cooked at too high a heat, or drained of fat before the spices go in
items.fix: Leave a little fat in the pan; it carries flavour. Add a splash of water when you add the spices and stir to loosen.

items.symptom: The taco shells go soft quickly
items.cause: Filled too early, or warm filling added before the shells have been heated
items.fix: Warm the shells right before serving and fill them at the table, not in the kitchen.

items.symptom: The shells keep falling apart when eaten
items.cause: Overfilled, or shells stored past their best
items.fix: Use about 2 tablespoons of beef per shell. Check the sell-by date on the shells; old shells become brittle.

items.cause: Not enough seasoning, or spices added too late
items.fix: Add the spices directly to the pan and let them cook for a minute before adding liquid; raw spice tastes dusty.

content.text: Swap the beef for turkey mince or, for a vegetarian version, use tinned black beans mashed roughly with the same spice mix. Soft corn tortillas work just as well if you prefer them to the crispy shells.

The hard-shell taco is an American creation. In Mexico, tacos are wrapped in soft corn tortillas. The crispy shell version was developed in the US through the mid-twentieth century, spreading via Tex-Mex cooking into mainstream American homes. Today it's one of the most common weeknight meals in American and British households.
